distractors.reason: We don't say 'listen strongly'. 'Strongly' describes force or belief, as in 'feel strongly' or 'agree strongly'.
We don't say 'listen quickly' to mean paying attention. 'Quickly' describes speed, as in 'run quickly'.
We don't say 'listen heavily'. 'Heavily' is used with things like 'rain heavily' or 'smoke heavily'.

example_sentence: Please listen ___ to the instructions before you start.
l1_interference: Po polsku przysłówek często stoi przed czasownikiem, np. 'uważnie słuchać', więc uczący się mogą powiedzieć 'carefully listen' zamiast 'listen carefully'. W angielskim przysłówek zwykle występuje po czasowniku.
explanation: In English, many verb + adverb collocations place the adverb after the verb. 'Carefully' describes the way someone pays attention when they listen.

related_collocations.example: She can speak English fluently after three years of study.
If you work hard, you will pass the exam.
I didn't sleep well last night because of the noise.

memory_tip: LISTEN + CAREFULLY = pay attention with care; in English the adverb normally comes after the verb.
